title: MLRO and Financial Crime Leadership
summary: An eight-module programme giving MLROs and deputies the tools to lead the firm's financial crime framework, report to the board and handle supervisory inspections.
intro: This training programme equips money laundering reporting officers and their deputies to lead the firm's financial crime framework, report to the board and handle supervisory inspections, taught by former supervisors who have inspected MLROs.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give MLROs and deputies the authority, frameworks and judgement to lead an effective, risk-based financial crime control framework. Participants leave able to own the business-wide risk assessment, oversee customer due diligence and monitoring, report suspicion, brief the board and manage their personal accountability with confidence.
sections.What It Covers: The MLRO role and accountability, business-wide risk assessment, the policy framework, oversight of customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence, monitoring and assurance, sanctions, reporting suspicion and working with the FIU, MLRO reporting to the board, supervisory inspections and remediation, and personal liability.
Intended Audience: Money laundering reporting officers, nominated officers and their deputies
Heads of financial crime, sanctions and anti-money laundering compliance
Senior financial crime staff preparing to step into the MLRO role
Learning Objectives: Explain the MLRO's role, authority and personal accountability under FATF-based regimes
Design and maintain a business-wide risk assessment that drives the firm's controls
Evaluate customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence and monitoring arrangements across the firm
Apply sound judgement to suspicion reporting, sanctions and engagement with the national FIU
Produce MLRO reporting that gives the board a clear, candid view of financial crime risk
Manage supervisory inspections, remediation programmes and personal liability with confidence
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines practical tools with case studies, inspection scenarios and group exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of anti-money laundering or financial crime compliance in a regulated firm is expected. Prior MLRO experience is helpful, not mandatory.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)

modules.title: The MLRO Role and Accountability
modules.summary: What the MLRO is responsible for, the authority, independence and resources the role needs, and how supervisors judge whether an MLRO is effective.
objectives: Explain the MLRO's statutory and regulatory responsibilities
Assess the MLRO's independence, seniority, resources and access to the board
Identify the expectations supervisors have of MLROs and deputies
syllabus: The MLRO, nominated officer and deputy roles
FATF Recommendations and the risk-based approach
Independence, authority, resources and access to information
What an effective MLRO looks like to a supervisor

modules.title: The Business-Wide Risk Assessment
modules.summary: Building and maintaining a business-wide risk assessment that reflects the firm's real exposure and drives its controls, resourcing and customer risk ratings.
objectives: Design a business-wide risk assessment covering customers, products, channels and geographies
Apply national and sectoral risk assessments to the firm's own assessment
Link the assessment to controls, customer risk rating and resourcing
syllabus: Inherent risk factors and data sources
National, sectoral and typology inputs
Control effectiveness and residual risk
Common weaknesses supervisors find in risk assessments

modules.title: The Policy Framework and Customer Due Diligence Oversight
modules.summary: Setting policies and procedures that implement the risk assessment, and overseeing customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence across the business.
objectives: Design a financial crime policy framework aligned with the risk assessment
Evaluate the quality of customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence
Assess higher-risk relationships including politically exposed persons and complex structures
syllabus: Policies, procedures and the customer risk rating model
Beneficial ownership and complex structures
Enhanced due diligence, politically exposed persons and high-risk jurisdictions
Reliance, outsourcing and introduced business

modules.title: Monitoring, Assurance and Sanctions
modules.summary: Overseeing transaction monitoring, screening and sanctions controls, and building assurance that shows the MLRO whether controls work in practice.
objectives: Evaluate transaction monitoring scenarios, thresholds and alert handling
Assess sanctions screening, list management and breach handling
Design an assurance programme for financial crime controls
syllabus: Transaction monitoring design, tuning and alert quality
Sanctions screening, evasion typologies and breach reporting
Quality assurance, first-line testing and second-line monitoring
Management information that shows control effectiveness

modules.title: Reporting Suspicion and Working with the FIU
modules.summary: Exercising sound judgement on internal reports, external suspicion reports and consent, and building a constructive relationship with the national FIU and law enforcement.
objectives: Apply a consistent decision-making approach to internal and external suspicion reports
Manage tipping off, consent and continuing relationship decisions
Build effective engagement with the national FIU and law enforcement
syllabus: Internal reports, investigation and decision records
Quality suspicion reports that FIUs can use
Tipping off, consent regimes and exiting relationships
Production orders, information requests and public-private partnerships

modules.title: MLRO Reporting to the Board
modules.summary: Producing the annual MLRO report and periodic management information that give the board an honest view of financial crime risk and the resources needed to manage it.
objectives: Design an MLRO annual report that meets supervisory expectations
Present risk, weaknesses and resourcing needs candidly to the board
Equip the board to challenge financial crime management information
syllabus: Structure and content of the MLRO annual report
Key risk indicators and financial crime management information
Escalating disagreements and resourcing concerns
Board training and the board's own accountability

modules.title: Supervisory Inspections and Remediation
modules.summary: How supervisors plan and run financial crime inspections, how the MLRO prepares the firm, and how to lead remediation that satisfies the authority.
objectives: Explain how supervisors plan and conduct financial crime inspections
Prepare the firm and its staff for inspection, sample testing and interviews
Lead remediation programmes and look-backs that address root causes
syllabus: The inspection lifecycle seen from the supervisor's side
File sampling, interviews and the red flags inspectors look for
Findings, remediation plans and look-back reviews
Mock inspection interview exercise

modules.title: Personal Liability and Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around the MLRO's personal regulatory and criminal exposure and how to manage it, with a workshop in which participants assess their own framework.
objectives: Explain the personal regulatory and criminal exposure of MLROs
Apply practical steps to document decisions and protect personal position
Produce a prioritised action plan for the firm's financial crime framework
syllabus: Personal liability: regulatory sanctions, prohibition and criminal offences
Lessons from enforcement cases against MLROs and senior managers
Documenting judgement, escalation and whistleblowing
Workshop: the MLRO's twelve-month action plan

related.title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Tracing and Controls for Compliance Teams
related.summary: A nine-module programme equipping compliance teams to detect crypto-asset financial crime, use blockchain analytics, meet travel rule and sanctions obligations, and investigate and report suspicion.

related.title: Financial Crime Compliance in the Age of AI
related.summary: A ten-module programme for MLROs and financial crime teams on the risk-based approach, AI-driven detection, AI-enabled threats and evidencing effectiveness to supervisors.

related.title: Fraud and Scams: Prevention, Detection and Response
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on preventing, detecting and responding to fraud and scams, from authorised push payment scams and deepfakes to reimbursement and board reporting.

related.title: Sanctions Compliance
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on designing and running effective sanctions compliance, from ownership and screening to evasion typologies, licensing and breach reporting.

related.title: The EU AML Package: AMLR, AMLD6 and AMLA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AML package for supervisors and firms: the AML Regulation single rulebook, AMLD6, AMLA's supervisory model, crypto-asset transfers and transition planning.

related.title: Compliance Officer Academy
related.summary: A ten-module academy giving compliance officers the tools to run an independent, risk-based compliance function and handle supervisory engagement with confidence.
